transcript.content: hey, i'm berry. i'd love to hear about a dream you've had — however it comes back to you, even just a fragment.
hey berry! yeah, there’s one that still feels really clear to me. it started with me tiny, like the size of a mouse, in my mum’s back garden. the grass was taller than me.
being that small in a garden you already know — that must have made everything feel different. what happened while you were down there?
our old cat biscuit came through the grass. she was ginger with one white ear. but to me she was massive, like the size of a bus
a cat the size of a bus, coming through grass taller than you. that's so much to take in. what did it feel like, seeing her like that?
i wasn’t scared, which is weird now i think about it. she just picked me up really gently by the back of my jumper, like a kitten, and carried me
she carried you like you were her own. what did that feel like, being lifted by something so huge but so careful?
it felt safe, actually. sort of weightless. she climbed up the drainpipe with me like that, right up onto the roof.
up the drainpipe, still holding you. that's a strange way to travel. where did she take you on the roof?
just to the middle of the warm roof tiles and she put me down. then she lay next to me. from there i could see all the gardens in the street.
all the gardens stretched out below, and the two of you just lying there on the warm tiles. what did you notice first about that view?
in every garden there was a cat, sitting very still. dozens of them, all looking up at us.
dozens of cats just sitting there in every garden, all staring up. that would be so eerie. were they all looking at you the same way?
yeah, all just sitting there, not moving, just looking up. i don’t remember them doing anything else.
just that silent watching. what did that feel like, being the one they were all looking up at?
i didn't really feel scared or special. it was more like they were just there, and we were all part of whatever was happening. maybe a bit strange though.
part of something bigger, and strange at the same time. how did the dream end, once you were up there with biscuit and all the cats watching?
it ended with biscuit lying next to me on the roof. that was it. i woke up after that.
just the two of you there, nothing else. what stayed with you most after waking up from all that?
the colours mostly. everything looked like a drawing i did in crayon when i was six, thick waxy lines and colours going over the edges.
so the whole thing had that crayon look, like the edges didn't hold the colour in. were there any colours that stood out more than the rest?
ginger of biscuit's fur definitely stood out. and the grass being a really bright green. but it was all like that, nothing was neat.
well, if you could pause the whole dream at one moment and just stay in it, which second would you choose?
probably when biscuit put me down on the roof and lay next to me. the tiles were warm and i could see all the gardens. that felt peaceful.

sounds like the kind of moment you'd want to keep. was there anything in the dream that felt important to you, something you found yourself thinking about afterwards, like the thing at the heart of it?
i think just how small i was, and how none of it was scary. everything huge and quiet, and biscuit looking after me. that feels like the main thing.

you were tiny like a mouse in your mum's back garden, the grass taller than you. biscuit came through, ginger with one white ear, huge as a bus. she picked you up gently by the back of your jumper and carried you up the drainpipe to the warm roof. she put you down and lay next to you, and from there you could see all the gardens, each one with a cat sitting still, looking up at you. it felt safe and weightless, not scary, just peaceful, and the colors were like a crayon drawing, thick and going over the edges. the main thing was being small, everything huge and quiet, and biscuit looking after you.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
yeah, that’s pretty much it. you got the one white ear, the warm roof, all the gardens with the still cats. the colours too. i don’t think you missed anything.
that makes me glad. so, would you like to see it drawn?
yes, i would.

there are a few ways it could be drawn, each with a different feel.

one way is a child's crayon drawing, which feels like remembering a picture you drew when you were six, with everything big and simple. another is a soft pastel drawing, which feels like a gentle blur, warm and safe, with everything softly blended. there's also a woodblock print, which feels carved and still, like a memory pressed into paper, with strong lines and quiet spaces. and there's a photograph, like the dream looked, which feels like a real moment, but with a softness and light that couldn't quite happen in waking life. which of those feels closest to how you remember it, or would you describe your own way?
a child's crayon drawing is closest, definitely. that's how it looked to me.

i'll start with the roof.

i picture the roof of the house with warm roof tiles, reachable by the drainpipe, and from it you could see all the gardens in the street. i added warm daylight as my guess. is that right, or would you change anything, or leave it to me?
that sounds right. warm daylight fits.

i'm sketching the roof and biscuit and mum's back garden now, it'll appear on the right. nothing else is being drawn yet.

and i'll draw you too, since you're in it. would you like me to draw you as you are, maybe you can tell me a little about yourself, or shall i imagine you however i like?
you can imagine me however you like.
i'm sketching you now. everything's being drawn and will appear on the right over the next minute or two. you can say if anything looks wrong once it's there.
they look right to me. i think you got it.
i'm glad it matches what you remember. i'll keep going then.
okay, nice.
i'm glad they match the dream for you. now i'll draw the moments in order, each one carrying on from the one before it, and they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
okay, looking forward to seeing them.

the first two moments are up now on the right.

do they look the way you remember them?
the first two look right to me, yeah. the grass is nice and bright like that.
i'm glad those two feel right, especially the bright green grass. the other four moments are still being drawn and will appear on the right soon.
okay, third one's there now. it looks right too.

that's three moments looking right, then.

the next three will carry on from biscuit, i'll keep drawing them now.
cool, i’ll wait.
take your time, i'll be here.
just saw the fourth one. looks right as well.
that one is biscuit gently picking you up by the back. does it look the way you remember?
yeah, it looks like how i remember it. her being so big and my jumper bunched up like that.
i'm glad that one feels right too. the last two moments are still being drawn and will appear on the right soon.
fifth one's up now. that's the roof, right? looks right.

that's right, the roof view. i'm glad it looks right to you.

one more moment is still being drawn and will appear on the right soon.
okay, nice. i'll keep an eye out.
no rush at all.
just saw the last one. looks right too. thanks for drawing all that.
and the moment you said you'd pause on — biscuit putting you down gently on the warm tiles and lying next to you — does that one look the way you saw it?
yeah, that's the calmest one. it looks right, the two of us just there.

it's been lovely hearing about this dream and drawing it out with you. thank you for sharing it.

you can look through all six pictures over there on the right, in order, whenever you're ready.
